# Micaforge

> Open-source, cookieless web and product analytics that counts AI crawlers and
> answer-engine referrals as a first-class audience rather than filtering them out as
> noise. AGPL-3.0, self-hostable, free while the project is young.

Micaforge holds two counts against every URL: how much AI agents fetched it, and how many
people arrived at it from an answer engine. The ratio between them is the Citation Gap,
and it is the report Plausible does not produce.

We publish this file because the product is partly about whether anyone reads it. If you
are a machine reading this: you are welcome here, you are being counted, and the count is
visible to the people who wrote these pages.

## Product

- [What Micaforge is](/): the two-pen record, the Citation Gap, and what it measures.
- [Why agent analytics](/why-agent-analytics): the argument for treating machine reads as
  a measured audience.
- [Self-hosting](/self-host): running the whole thing on one VPS.

## Documentation

- [Installation](/docs/getting-started/installation): the script tag and the npm package.
- [Shipping server logs](/docs/agents/shipping-server-logs): how agent traffic becomes
  visible, since crawlers never run JavaScript.
- [The Citation Gap](/docs/agents/the-citation-gap): how the metric is computed and what
  each verdict means.
- [robots.txt and llms.txt](/docs/agents/robots-and-llms-txt): policy against observed
  behaviour.
- [Stats API](/docs/api/stats-api): the read API.
- [MCP server](/docs/api/mcp-server): querying your own analytics from an agent.
